summary: Compromise through dependencies, package resolution, build scripts, CI/CD workflows, container base images and release signing, established from lockfiles, SBOMs, workflow files, build scripts and OSV/Scorecard evidence.
looks_for: GitHub Actions, reusable workflows and container images referenced by mutable tag or branch instead of a full commit SHA or digest
pull_request_target or workflow_run workflows that check out and build the untrusted head ref with secrets or a write-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN available
workflow run: steps interpolating attacker-controlled expressions (issue titles, PR bodies, branch names, commit messages) directly into shell
over-broad workflow permissions (write-all or unset defaults), secrets exposed to fork builds, self-hosted runners serving public-repo jobs
manifests without lockfiles, lockfiles out of sync with manifests, version ranges on direct dependencies, or install commands that ignore the lockfile
dependency confusion exposure: internal package names resolvable from a public registry, extra-index-url or multiple registries without scoping
install-time code: npm pre/postinstall scripts, setup.py and build backends, Gradle/Maven plugins, go generate, Cargo build.rs from third parties
curl | sh, remote script or binary downloads in Dockerfiles, Makefiles and CI steps without checksum or signature verification
dependencies with known exploited or critical OSV advisories reachable from shipped code, and abandoned or single-maintainer packages flagged by Scorecard
release and publish paths without provenance or signing (no SLSA provenance, cosign or sigstore signature, unprotected release tags)
vendored, copied or generated code with no recorded upstream origin, version or regeneration step
source-to-artifact divergence: build steps that fetch, patch or generate code not present in the reviewed tree
preconditions: the attacker controls or can influence an input the build trusts: a public package name, an upstream repository, a PR from a fork, a mutable tag, or a download URL
the build or install resolves that input without pinning it to an immutable identity (commit SHA, digest, lockfile integrity hash, checksum)
the influenced step runs with something worth taking: repository or registry secrets, write tokens, signing keys, deploy credentials, or it produces the shipped artifact
for dependency confusion: an internal package name is unclaimed or claimable on the public registry the resolver consults
for a vulnerable dependency: the vulnerable version is the one resolved in the lockfile or SBOM and the affected code path is reachable from the shipped application
proof_obligations: the workflow, Dockerfile, build script or manifest line at file:line containing the unpinned reference, untrusted interpolation or unsafe trigger
for CI: the trigger (pull_request_target, workflow_run, issue_comment) plus the checkout of untrusted code plus the secret or token scope available to that job, each cited
for dependencies: the resolved version from the lockfile or Syft SBOM, and the OSV or Grype advisory id matching that exact version
for reachability: the import or call site at file:line of the vulnerable function or module, or an explicit statement that reachability was not established
for dependency confusion: the registry configuration (.npmrc, pip.conf, settings.xml, nuget.config) at file:line and the unscoped internal package name
for remote downloads: the fetch at file:line and the absence of a checksum, signature or pinned digest on the same step
the relevant Scorecard check result (Pinned-Dependencies, Token-Permissions, Dangerous-Workflow, Branch-Protection, Signed-Releases) when it was run, or a recorded gap when it was not
false_positive_traps: dev-only, test-only or build-only dependencies that are not bundled or shipped, reported as runtime exposure
OSV or Grype advisories matched on a manifest range while the lockfile or SBOM resolves a fixed version
advisories against a function or optional feature the application never imports or enables
actions from the same organization or first-party GitHub actions (actions/*) flagged as untrusted without a concrete takeover path; they still count as unpinned if not SHA-pinned
pull_request_target workflows that only label or comment and never check out or execute the head ref
lockfile drift that is only a formatting, integrity-algorithm or platform-specific optional-dependency difference
curl downloads followed by a checksum or signature check on a later line of the same step or script
private registries configured as the only index with scoped names, where public resolution cannot occur
must_not: report a CVE or OSV match as exploitable without the resolved version and a reachability statement
treat an unpinned reference as a compromise; it is exposure to one, and the finding must say so
publish, install, resolve or execute any package, action or script from the target during review
